sentences.text: Kamuysaurus was a herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur found in Late Cretaceous marine deposits near Mukawa, Hokkaido, Japan. This animal measured approximately 8 meters in length.
Its weight is estimated at 4 or 5.3 tonnes, depending on whether it was bipedal or quadrupedal.

The describing authors identified three unique derived characters, or autapomorphies, for the species. A unique feature is a notch on the quadrate bone located at three-quarters of the shaft length from the top. Neural spines on the sixth through thirteenth back vertebrae are inclined forward.
An amateur paleontologist discovered the tail of a Kamuysaurus at Shirafunezawa Creek in 2003.
An entire Kamuysaurus skeleton was uncovered by museum teams in 2013 and 2014.
The species Kamuysaurus japonicus was named and described in 2019 by a team led by Professor Yoshitsugu Kobayashi.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — represents an adult individual at least nine years old.
Researchers suggest the carcass was likely washed into the sea.
Kamuysaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
The time range for the genus is listed as the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
